messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — we're seeing periodic 429s from our Dedicated pool (pool id: pool-rw-07z) during our nightly enrichment job. We have reserved capacity, SLA <-> billing shows committed units available. Logs show short bursts at ~6am UTC that push QPS up briefly and then requests get 429s for ~30s. Any idea?
ian_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a small sample of the headers you see with the 429? Particularly the x-rate-limit headers and the request_id.
acme_ops: Sure, sample headers below (sanitized):
```
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
x-rate-limit-limit: 3000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 167
x-dedicated-pool-id: pool-rw-07z
x-slo-tier: reserved
status: 429
```
ian_support: thanks. That remaining=0 + short reset suggests a token-bucket exhaustion during bursts. Is the job very spiky? Do you stream responses or fire many short calls?
acme_ops: It's a mix — main loop spawns 200 concurrent short generation jobs (each ~2-4 tokens avg per request), runs for ~3 minutes. We expected the reserved pool to absorb that. SLA on the contract says 99.9% for throughput.
maya_sre: pinging eng/runtime — this looks like a rate-smoothing mismatch. Dedicated reserved pools have two controls: per-pool sustained QPS and a burst allowance window. If the burst window is too small, rapid fanout can deplete tokens quickly and cause 429s even with enough aggregate capacity.
devon_eng: Confirming. We saw a recent config change to the rate-smoother defaults for the eu-west clusters (smaller bucket_time_ms). For pool-rw-07z the bucket_time was reduced to 5s which lowers how much instantaneous burst you can absorb.
acme_ops: Is that change recent? We didn't change anything on our side.
devon_eng: Yes, rolled 2026-02-28 as a perf optimization for streaming latencies. It reduced some long-tail p99 but decreased the burst headroom for certain pools. Noted — bad interaction with high-fanout short requests.
zoe_acct: From accounts side: the customer has reserved units adequate for the nightly peak, billing not the issue. We should treat as operational config.
ian_support: To help repro / mitigate: 1) can you run a controlled fanout test using our stress endpoint with your service token so we can reproduce the exact request pattern? 2) please gather connection-level telemetry: upstream concurrency, average tokens requested and headers for a failing sample.
acme_ops: I can run a test at 2026-03-03 06:00 UTC. Test plan: spawn 200 parallel curl jobs to our inference route for 3 minutes, 50ms delay between spawns. Payload is short prompt. Should I include streaming=false in the test?
maya_sre: Yes include streaming=false to simulate short stateless calls. Also please add `X-Debug-Mode: true` header to capture the backend shard selection header.
acme_ops: OK. I'll post logs after the run.
devon_eng: Meanwhile immediate mitigations we can apply from infra side: - bump the bucket_time_ms for pool-rw-07z from 5s to 30s to increase burst headroom (low risk). - temporarily route traffic to fallback variant `redwood-mini-1` which has more aggressive burst capacity. We can enable either while we investigate long-term config. Which do you prefer?
acme_ops: Prefer infra bump first, then fallback if still flaky. Avoid fallback unless necessary.
ian_support: Noted. I'll open a change request. devon — estimated time to bump?
devon_eng: Can do a hot-config update; I'll schedule for the test window + 5m. If we see 429s after bump we'll flip routing.
zoe_acct: I'll keep the customer updated — will note that this is an ops config change and not a billing/commit issue.
acme_ops: Test completed. Attached condensed trace (small paste):
```
[06:00:12] concurrent=200 qps=650 tokens_per_req=3
[06:00:39] 429 start (token_exhaust) shard=eu-01 node=node-7
[06:01:10] 200 ok resume
p95 latency spike to 980ms during window
```
maya_sre: This reproduces the pattern. devon — can you confirm whether token refills are per-node or global for the pool? Might matter due to shard hot spots.
devon_eng: Refill is global per-pool, but allocation happens per-node. Hot-sharding can cause a node-local depletion even if global tokens exist (we have a shard smoothing step but it's tuned low). We'll increase smoothing and bucket time.
ian_support: Action items: - devon to bump bucket_time_ms -> 30s and smoothing -> +1 (owner: devon, ETA: 20m) - ian to monitor the pool and open an incident if 429s persist (owner: ian, ETA: 1h) - acme_ops to run one more quick fanout after infra change (owner: acme_ops, ETA: after change) - zoe to notify the account (owner: zoe, ETA: now)
devon_eng: Change applied to pool-rw-07z. bucket_time_ms=30000 smoothing=+1. Rolling config across eu cluster now.
ian_support: Monitoring graphs show drop in 429s after config join. Can everyone verify from their side? :eyes: 
acme_ops: Quick run: no 429s in 10m window. p95 latency improved slightly. Thanks.
zoe_acct: I'll convert this to a follow-up RFC to make the burst headroom change permanent for similar pools, and we'll update runbooks with a recommended test pattern for customers doing high fanout short calls.
acme_ops: Appreciate the quick help. We'll keep an eye and report if anything recurs. :+1:
